title: Alignment Microfestival runbook + exec ask compass (Q4 planning draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight runbook for a 3-day asynchronous + 1 synchronous microfestival to align the company for Q4 planning and exec ask prioritization. The goal is to produce a concise set of executable priorities (top 3 company bets), a trimmed OKR draft to take to exec review, and a short all-staff primer that surfaces tradeoffs and staff asks.

Why a microfestival format?
- Short, bounded, accessible across time zones
- Mix of async artifacts (one-pagers, tiny demos) + one synchronous all-staff sync for commitment consent
- Encourages experiments in cadence and clearer decision hygiene (decide fast, document faster)

High-level outcomes (success signals):
1) Exec-approved top 3 company bets for Q4 with owners and sizing (committed by execs within 48h of festival close).
2) Draft OKRs trimmed to no more than 6 company-level objectives with measurable signals and one fallback priority.
3) All-staff primer (1-page) that explains why each top bet exists, what success looks like, and where to escalate.
4) A prioritized roll-out map for Dedicated and Private customers that captures capacity, SLAs, and sales enablement asks.

Timing and format
- Day -7 to -1 (Pre): Collect one-pagers from each leadership pod. Template below.
- Day 0 (Async synth): Core team synthesizes one-pagers into a short candidate slate.
- Day 1 (Async contributions): Teams add commentary, risks, counterproposals inline.
- Day 2 (Synchronous): 90-minute all-staff + decision window (execs sign-off).
- Day +2 (Post): Publish final OKRs, exec brief, and squad-level next steps.

One-pager template (250–400 words)
- Title / short label
- Problem we solve (1–2 sentences)
- Proposed bet / deliverable (what we ship or change)
- Customer impact (metric(s) or signal)
- Cost / capacity implications (GPU-hours estimate, infra changes)
- Key risks and mitigations
- Required exec decision(s) (yes/no gating)

Roles and responsibilities
- Festival lead: Priya Nair (or delegate) — orchestration, synth, and final packaging.
- Synthesis team: Ethan Ramirez, Grace Park, Noah Thompson — compile one-pagers, surface conflicts.
- Comms lead: Maya Singh — one-pager template distribution, primer, publishing.
- Engineering capacity liaison: Omar El-Amin — quick feasibility checks and capacity sizing.
- Execs: Founders + CTO + Head of Product — decision authority during Day 2 window.

Draft company-level OKRs (working)
Objective A: Improve inference economics and predictability for customers- Key Result A1: Reduce median p95 token cost (hosted) by 18% across top-10 tail prompts by end of Q4- Key Result A2: Ship two model-variant fallback policies with telemetry and automatic routing for 90% of requests- Key Result A3: Publish three verified performance profiles for common open models in the catalog

Objective B: Increase enterprise adoption of Dedicated and Private deployments- Key Result B1: Close 3 new Dedicated contracts (>$250k ARR each) with SLA commitments- Key Result B2: Deliver Private deployment on-boarding playbook and 24h support pilot for 2 customers- Key Result B3: Decrease mean-time-to-deploy (Private) from 12 days to 6 days for pilot customers

Objective C: Reduce production incidents and improve runtime reliability- Key Result C1: Decrease sev1 incidents by 40% quarter-over-quarter- Key Result C2: Introduce rollout canary automation across 100% of model deploy pipelines

Notes on draft OKRs: these are intentionally narrow. During the microfestival we will debate which KRs are leading indicators vs vanity metrics. Expect teams to propose alternative signals (latency SLOs, P99 vs P95, cost-per-embedding).

Run-of-show (Day 2 synchronous 90 minutes)
- 00:00–00:05 Welcome and framing (Priya)
- 00:05–00:15 Exec synthesis of candidate slate (Founders/CTO)
- 00:15–00:35 Lightning rebuttal / clarifying questions from pods (pre-submitted + live)
- 00:35–00:60 Decision window: execs mark each candidate as Accept / Revise / Reject with a short rationale
- 00:60–00:80 Commitments: assign owners, quick sizing, and next 14-day milestones
- 00:80–00:90 Close, publication plan, and three immediate team-level asks (Comms)

Comms and artifacts to publish
- Exec brief (top 2 pages) summarizing decisions and tradeoffs — target: published Day+1
- Public primer for company (1 page + Q&A) — target: published Day+1
- OKR doc with ownership and measurable signals — target: Day+2
- Triage backlog for items labeled "follow" or "deferred" with next review date — target: Day+7

Open questions and friction points (to resolve before Day 0)
- Capacity: do we allow temporary burst capacity to avoid blocking high-impact launches? (link: JIRA RDW-3301)
- Pricing: should cost-savings KR include absolute dollar measures or relative % compared to last quarter?
- Private onboarding SLA: what is the minimal set of security controls required for pilot (KMS, audit logs)?
- Eval gating: what grade on quality regression evals is required to approve a model variant for routing?

Risk register (top 5)
1) Exec indecision leads to long tail of follow-ups — mitigation: time-box decisions and escalate conflicts to a small arbitration panel.
2) Underestimated infra cost for quantization rollout — mitigation: require capacity liaison sign-off on cost estimate.
3) Poor cross-team participation — mitigation: assign two skip-level owners per pod and run pre-festival prep checkpoints.
4) Message mismatch between product and sales for Dedicated offering changes — mitigation: require a 30-minute sales alignment slot as part of post-microfestival comms.
5) Regulatory or compliance blockers for Private pilots — mitigation: route to Security & Compliance with a 48h expedited review path.

Immediate next steps (by end of week)
- Distribute one-pager template and start collection (Owner: Priya)
- Synthesis team to create candidate slate and post to Confluence (Owner: Ethan)
- Book Day 2 synchronous slot (global-friendly) and reserve recording + live captions (Owner: Maya)
- Security & Compliance: provide checklist for Private pilot gating (Owner: Omar to coordinate with Security)

Appendix: quick templates
- One-pager link: confluence.redwood.internal/display/ALIGN/One-Pager+Template
- Okrs doc link (working): confluence.redwood.internal/display/OKR/Company+Draft+Q4
- Jira intake: RDW-2345 (microfestival orchestration epic)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally concise and action-oriented. Please add only concrete content to one-pagers: avoid long histories.
- If you are a pod lead and cannot contribute a one-pager by Day -1, assign a delegate and add a note in the Confluence page.
- Flag any hard constraints (legal, compliance, major infra commits) by adding a comment on the candidate slate under the "constraints" section.

Unresolved items for exec workshop:
- Define acceptance criteria for KR A1 (cost reduction): should include token-type stratification and a post-deploy monitoring window.
- Confirm the commercial packaging for Dedicated (monthly vs annual pricing) to quantify ARR targets.

Contact and escalation
